input.quote: 7.7 If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date, Customer shall pay Vendor, as liquidated damages and not as a penalty, an amount equal to fifteen percent of the annual Fees for each week the invoice remains unpaid.
input.rationale: Clause 7.7 is an express Customer-payable liquidated damages provision triggered by a minor breach (payment ten days late) at fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, which compounds beyond the remaining contract value and is walk-away territory, not merely short of preferred. It is the only Customer-payable liquidated or penalty amount in the document (§ 10 imposes no termination fee, and § 27 permits termination "without penalty"), so no fallback early-termination-fee bargain exists to preserve. We therefore delete the liquidated damages mechanic and state the preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties; Vendor retains its § 7.3 and general remedies for genuine non-payment.

mappings.element: Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties.

proposal.summary: Replace Customer-payable late-payment liquidated damages with an unconditional no-LD statement
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages against us — 15% of annual Fees per week of late payment is punitive and far exceeds any loss. We have replaced clause 7.7 with our preferred position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties; if a liquidated amount is unavoidable, our fallback is an early-termination fee capped at three months' fees as the sole liquidated amount.
